cases.name: digest-vectors
cases.notes: §11.5 canonical JSON and the digest, pinned byte for byte: key order by UTF-8 bytes (`z` before `é`), no whitespace, `null` kept; numbers — integral below 2^53 without a fraction (`1.0` → `1`, `-0` → `0`), others by ECMAScript Number::toString (`1.5`, `0.30000000000000004`, `1e+21`, `1e-7`, `9007199254740992`, `1.7976931348623157e+308`, `123456789012345680000`); strings — only `"`, `\\` and U+0000–U+001F escaped (`\b \f \n \r \t`, else `\u00xx` lower-case), `/` and non-ASCII literal; the last vector is an empty plan core — its `digest` is the `plan_id` a planner must give it (`execute-plan-edited-is-plan-mismatch` reports the same value as `actual`). Then the empty core under `planner_v` p1 (2.3), p2 (3.0) and p3 (3.1), and the empty p3 core with a zero-hit `selection` (§11.8; `select-zero-hits-commit-null`'s plan has that `plan_id`) — the digests §11.5 quotes.

cases.name: sugar-leader-target-identity
cases.notes: §11.8 Sugar, the worked example spelled with the leader: `into: "-> project"` is a whole-target expression (the identity the value names — a path string, so a document) and the markdown a template literal; the templates desugar to `{ oqx }` before admission, so the plan's `effects`/`opset` are `select-rollup-two-workstreams-one-hub`'s (the `plan_id` differs only through `selection.templates`, recorded AS WRITTEN); `execute` commits the same bytes with the written templates in the intent record.

cases.notes: §11.3 (3.6, "Frontmatter entries"): `set frontmatter.<k>` edits ONE part. The flow list, the quoted string, the comment that documents `cues` and the trailing comment keep their bytes across a `set` of `layer`, an `unset` of `status`, and a `set` of the new key `owner` (inserted after the last entry, before the trailing comment); only `layer`'s own line is re-rendered. cases.name: set-fm-continuations-and-comments
cases.notes: §11.3 "Frontmatter entries": the split rule over one frontmatter — the comment and blank line before the first entry are a key-less part; a flow list, a column-0 block sequence, a block scalar with a blank line inside, a nested mapping, an empty value and a `null` value are each one entry with their continuation lines; a comment between two entries leads the FOLLOWING key; the trailing comment and blank line are a key-less part. Setting `list` re-renders only its lines (the emitter writes an indented block sequence) and setting `nothing` keeps `# who owns it` above the quoted key; every other byte is as authored.
